subject: Science
theme: Electric current and its chemical effects

lba_qa.q: You test plain distilled water and salt water with an LED tester. The LED glows in salt water but not in distilled water. Why this difference?
lba_qa.a:
The difference is that salt water has dissolved IONS, but distilled water does not.

The science:
1. To conduct electricity, a liquid needs charged particles (ions)
2. Distilled water is PURE — it has no dissolved salts → no ions → does NOT conduct → LED stays off ✅
3. Salt water has dissolved salt that splits into ions → it conducts electricity → LED glows ✅

So a liquid conducts only if it has ions in it.

This is why pure (distilled) water is a poor conductor but salty or impure water conducts well.

lba_qa.q: A tester with a bulb does not glow even when current flows through a weak conducting liquid, but an LED in the tester does glow. Why is an LED better for testing?
lba_qa.a:
An LED is better because it lights up even with a VERY SMALL current.

The science:
1. A bulb needs a fairly LARGE current to glow brightly
2. Through a weak conductor, only a tiny current flows → the bulb may not glow ✅
3. An LED (Light Emitting Diode) lights up even with a very tiny current ✅

So for testing weakly conducting liquids, an LED shows a result where a bulb would seem to fail.

Note: an LED must be connected the correct way round (it has + and - ends) to work.

lba_qa.q: When current is passed through salty water, you notice gas bubbles forming on the electrodes. What does this prove about electric current?
lba_qa.a:
The gas bubbles prove the CHEMICAL EFFECT of electric current.

What happens:
1. When current passes through a conducting liquid (electrolyte), a chemical reaction takes place ✅
2. This reaction can release gases at the electrodes → gas bubbles appear ✅
3. Other signs include a metal deposit on an electrode or a colour change in the solution

So electric current does not just produce heat or light — it can also cause CHEMICAL CHANGES.

The gas bubbles on the electrodes are clear evidence of this chemical effect of electric current.

lba_qa.q: A shiny gold-coloured layer is put on a cheap metal bangle using electricity. What is this process called and how does it work?
lba_qa.a:
This process is ELECTROPLATING — coating one metal with a layer of another using electricity.

How it works:
1. The object to be coated and a piece of the coating metal are placed in a salt solution of that metal
2. Electric current is passed through the solution ✅
3. The chemical effect of the current deposits a thin layer of the desired metal onto the object ✅

Uses of electroplating:
- Making cheap jewellery look golden
- Coating iron with zinc/chromium to prevent rusting

So electroplating uses the chemical effect of current to give a metal coating.

lba_qa.q: Iron objects used in bridges and gates are coated with a thin layer of zinc. Why is this done?
lba_qa.a:
Iron is coated with ZINC to PREVENT RUSTING (this is called galvanisation).

The reason:
1. Iron rusts easily when exposed to air and moisture ✅
2. Rusting weakens and damages the iron
3. A thin zinc coating protects the iron from air and water
4. So the iron does not rust and lasts much longer ✅

This zinc coating is often done by electroplating.

So coating iron with zinc protects bridges, gates and pipes from rusting and increases their life.

lba_qa.q: Tin cans are used to store food. The iron cans are coated with a layer of tin, not left as plain iron. Why use tin?
lba_qa.a:
Iron cans are coated with TIN because tin is safer for food and does not rust.

The reasons:
1. Plain iron rusts and would spoil the food
2. Tin is LESS REACTIVE than iron ✅
3. The tin coating stops the food from touching the iron
4. So the food does not react with the metal and stays safe ✅

So tin-coating (done by electroplating) keeps stored food from spoiling and protects the iron can from rusting.

This is why food tins are tin-plated iron.

lba_qa.q: When a fire breaks out, firefighters first switch off the main electricity supply before spraying water. Why is this step so important?
lba_qa.a:
This is important because WATER CONDUCTS ELECTRICITY and could cause shocks.

The reason:
1. Ordinary water (with its dissolved salts) is a good conductor of electricity ✅
2. If water is sprayed while the supply is on, electricity can pass through the water
3. This could give dangerous electric shocks to the firefighters ✅

So the main supply is switched off first to make the water safe to use.

This is also why we never use water on an electrical fire until the power is cut. Safety first.

lba_qa.q: Bicycle handles and wheel rims are coated with shiny chromium. Why is chromium used for this?
lba_qa.a:
CHROMIUM is used to coat bicycle parts for several good reasons.

Why chromium:
1. It has a bright, attractive SHINE (luster) ✅
2. It does NOT rust or corrode easily
3. It is hard and resists scratches ✅

Why not make the whole part of chromium:
- Chromium is expensive, so only a thin coating is applied (by electroplating)

So a thin chromium layer makes the cheaper metal underneath look shiny, protects it from rust, and resists scratches — perfect for handles and rims.

lba_qa.q: Two testers are dipped, one in tap water and one in sea water. The magnetic needle deflects MORE in sea water. Explain why.
lba_qa.a:
The needle deflects more in sea water because sea water conducts electricity BETTER.

The science:
1. A larger current makes the magnetic needle deflect more (magnetic effect of current)
2. Sea water has a HIGH amount of dissolved salts → many ions → conducts well → large current ✅
3. Tap water has only a SMALL amount of dissolved salts → fewer ions → conducts less → small current

So more salt = better conductor = more current = greater deflection. ✅

That is why the needle deflects more in the salty sea water than in tap water.

lba_qa.q: Rainwater can conduct a little electricity and make a tester's needle deflect, but pure distilled water cannot. Why the difference?
lba_qa.a:
The difference is the presence of dissolved salts (impurities).

The science:
1. To conduct electricity, water needs dissolved ions
2. RAINWATER picks up small amounts of dust, gases and salts from the air ✅
3. These give it a few ions, so it conducts a little and the needle deflects
4. DISTILLED water is pure — it has NO dissolved salts → no ions → does not conduct ✅

So even slightly impure water (rain, tap) conducts, but pure distilled water does not.

This is why we should treat rainwater as a conductor for safety.

lba_mcq.q: Priya tests salt water and distilled water with an LED tester. The LED glows only in salt water because salt water:
options: Has dissolved ions that conduct electricity
lba_mcq.explanation: Salt water contains dissolved ions that carry current, so it conducts and lights the LED. Pure distilled water has no ions and does not conduct.

lba_mcq.q: To test whether a very weakly conducting liquid carries current, an LED works better than a bulb because the LED:
options: Glows even with a very small current
lba_mcq.explanation: An LED lights up even with a very tiny current, so it can detect conduction in weak conductors where a bulb might not glow.

lba_mcq.q: Gas bubbles appear on the electrodes when current passes through a conducting solution. This is evidence of the:
lba_mcq.explanation: When current passes through an electrolyte, a chemical reaction occurs, releasing gas at the electrodes. This is the chemical effect of electric current.

lba_mcq.q: A cheap iron ring is given a shiny gold coating using electric current. This process is called:
lba_mcq.explanation: Electroplating uses the chemical effect of electric current to deposit a thin layer of one metal (like gold) onto another object.

lba_mcq.q: Iron gates and bridges are coated with a thin layer of zinc mainly to:
options: Change their colour for beauty only
lba_mcq.explanation: A zinc coating (galvanisation) protects iron from air and moisture, preventing rusting and making the structures last longer.

lba_mcq.q: Food storage cans are made of iron coated with tin rather than plain iron because tin:
options: Is less reactive and keeps the food safe
lba_mcq.explanation: Tin is less reactive than iron, so coating the can with tin stops the food from reacting with the metal and prevents rusting, keeping food safe.

lba_mcq.q: Firefighters switch off the main power before spraying water on a fire because:
options: Water conducts electricity and could give shocks
lba_mcq.explanation: Ordinary water conducts electricity, so spraying it on a live circuit can cause dangerous shocks. The supply is switched off first for safety.

lba_mcq.q: Bicycle handles are coated with chromium mainly because chromium:
options: Is shiny, resists rust and scratches
lba_mcq.explanation: Chromium gives a bright shine, resists corrosion and scratches, so a thin chromium coating protects and beautifies bicycle handles and rims.

lba_mcq.q: A tester's magnetic needle deflects more in sea water than in tap water. This shows that sea water:
options: Is a better conductor due to more dissolved salts
lba_mcq.explanation: Sea water has many dissolved salts (ions), so it conducts more current, causing a larger deflection of the magnetic needle than tap water.

lba_mcq.q: Distilled water does NOT conduct electricity, but tap water does. The reason is that tap water:
options: Contains dissolved salts that provide ions
lba_mcq.explanation: Tap water has dissolved salts that provide ions to carry current, so it conducts. Pure distilled water has no dissolved salts and does not conduct.
